stem: Which report format displays records in a plain list with no grouping or subtotals?

options.text: Tabular
Summary
Matrix
Joined

explanation: Tabular reports are simple lists, like a spreadsheet. Summary reports add grouping and subtotals.

stem: A manager wants opportunities grouped by stage with subtotals for each stage. Which format fits?

options.text: Summary
Tabular
Joined
None, a dashboard is needed

explanation: Summary reports group rows by a field and show subtotals.

stem: A manager wants Amount by owner in rows and by quarter in columns. Which format fits?

options.text: Matrix
Tabular
Summary
Joined

explanation: A matrix groups by both rows and columns, like a pivot table.

stem: Which report format lets you show opportunities and cases side by side in separate blocks?

options.text: Joined
Matrix
Summary
Tabular

explanation: Joined reports combine up to five blocks, each from a report type, matched on shared fields.

stem: Which of these cannot be used as the source report for a dashboard component?

options.text: A joined report
A summary report
A matrix report
A tabular report with a row limit

explanation: Joined reports cannot feed dashboard components. Use summary or matrix reports for charts.

objective: Explain how a report type works
stem: What does the report type determine?

options.text: Which objects and fields the report can use
Who can see the report once it has been saved
How often the report refreshes its data
Which dashboard the report appears on

explanation: The report type is the template that defines the available objects, relationships and fields.

stem: The sales director wants a report listing all accounts, including those with no opportunities. How should the custom report type relate Accounts to Opportunities?

options.text: "A" records with or without "B" records
"A" records with "B" records, which leaves out the ones with no "B"
"B" records only, with the "A" records that they belong to
Use a joined report, because standard types cannot list both

explanation: "With or without" returns every primary record. "With" returns only primary records that have related ones.

stem: What does the "Accounts with Opportunities" relationship return?

options.text: Only accounts that have at least one opportunity
All accounts, whether or not they have an opportunity
Only opportunities that have no account linked
Accounts that have no opportunities at all

explanation: "With" is an inner join: records with no related records are left out.

stem: How many objects can be linked in a single custom report type?

options.text: Four
Two
Six
Ten

explanation: A custom report type can include a primary object and up to three more, so four in total.

stem: A custom report type is set to In Development. Who can use it?

options.text: Only users who can manage it (admins) until it is deployed
All users who have access to the reports tab
No one, until the report type is deleted and rebuilt
Only external users logged in through an Experience Cloud site

explanation: In Development hides the report type from regular users. Set it to Deployed to make it available.

objective: Use filters, bucket fields and formulas
stem: Which feature finds accounts that have no activities in the last 30 days?

options.text: A cross filter with "without" activities
A bucket field that groups accounts by activity count
A summary formula that adds up the activities
A dashboard filter on the activity date field

explanation: A cross filter includes or excludes records based on related records, such as accounts without activities.

objective: Use filters, bucket fields and formulas
stem: What does a bucket field let you do?

options.text: Group values into categories without writing a formula
Combine two reports into a single joined report
Store data from a report in a custom object
Schedule a report to run at a set time

explanation: A bucket field groups values, such as amounts into Small, Medium and Large, directly in the report.

objective: Use filters, bucket fields and formulas
stem: Which formula type calculates a value for each individual record in a report?

options.text: Row-level formula
Summary formula
Roll-up summary
Validation formula

explanation: A row-level formula works per record. A summary formula works on grouped totals.

objective: Use filters, bucket fields and formulas
stem: The PREVGROUPVAL function is used in which kind of report formula?

options.text: Summary formula
Row-level formula
Validation rule
Flow formula

explanation: PREVGROUPVAL compares a grouped value with the previous group, so it belongs in summary formulas.

objective: Explain how sharing and folders affect reports
stem: A regional manager and the CEO open the same report. The manager sees fewer rows. Why?

options.text: Reports run as the viewer, so the sharing model limits the rows each person sees
The report is broken for managers and needs to be rebuilt by an admin
The manager's folder has fewer records in it than the CEO's folder
Reports only ever show the first 50 rows to users who are managers

explanation: Reports show only the records the viewer can access through sharing and field-level security.

objective: Explain how sharing and folders affect reports
stem: Which statement about report folders is true?

options.text: Folder access controls who can open, edit or manage the report, not which records they can see
Folder access overrides the sharing model for every record in the report
Folders give access to all the records that appear in the report
Folders can only be shared with one user at a time, never with groups

explanation: A folder decides access to the report itself. The data is still limited by the user's record access.

objective: Explain how sharing and folders affect reports
stem: Which TWO can a report folder be shared with? (Choose 2)

options.text: Roles
Public groups
Page layouts
Record types

explanation: Folders can be shared with individual users, roles and public groups, each with Viewer, Editor or Manager access.

objective: Explain how sharing and folders affect reports
stem: Which folder access level lets a user edit and share the folder's contents?

options.text: Manager
Viewer
Reader
Subscriber

explanation: Folder access levels are Viewer, Editor and Manager. Managers can also change who the folder is shared with.

stem: What does a reporting snapshot do?

options.text: Runs a report on a schedule and saves the results to a custom object
Takes a screenshot of a dashboard each week and files it in a folder
Backs up the whole org on a schedule and stores the files
Emails the report as a PDF to each user every Monday

explanation: A reporting snapshot stores results from a tabular or summary report in a custom object, so you can report on trends over time.

stem: Historical trend reporting is available for which TWO objects? (Choose 2)

options.text: Opportunities
Cases
Accounts
Contacts

explanation: Historical trend reporting covers opportunities, cases and forecasts.

stem: The director wants to see how total pipeline changed week by week over the last quarter. Which tool is designed for this?

options.text: A reporting snapshot or historical trend reporting
A bucket field that groups opportunities by size
A joined report that shows the current pipeline
A cross filter that excludes closed opportunities

explanation: Standard reports show data as of now. Snapshots and historical trend reporting store or track past values.

stem: A user wants an email each Monday only if open pipeline falls below a target. Which feature fits?

options.text: A report subscription with a condition
A dashboard filter set to the pipeline target
A reporting snapshot that saves the pipeline each week
A matrix report that shows pipeline by month

explanation: Report subscriptions can email results on a schedule and can include conditions that must be met before the email is sent.

objective: Use filters, bucket fields and formulas
stem: Which filter lets viewers narrow results to the current quarter using a date field?

options.text: The standard date range filter
A bucket field that groups the records by quarter
A summary formula that finds the current quarter
A report type that is limited to one quarter

explanation: Standard filters include a date field and range, such as Current FQ.

objective: Use filters, bucket fields and formulas
stem: Filter logic such as 1 AND (2 OR 3) lets you:

options.text: Combine field filters in a custom way
Group rows in a matrix report by the fields chosen
Control which folders a user can open
Schedule the report to run at a set time

explanation: Filter logic uses the numbered filters to control how they combine.

objective: Explain how sharing and folders affect reports
stem: Which statement about the report type and a user's field access is true?

options.text: A field appears in the report only if the report type includes it and the user has access to it
Every field on the object always appears in any report, whatever the type
Field-level security is ignored when users run reports they can open
Users can see any field in a report they open, even without field access

explanation: A report shows fields that the report type offers and that the viewer's field-level security allows.

stem: A manager needs accounts that have no opportunities. Which report setup fits?

options.text: A custom report type with Accounts with or without Opportunities
A summary report on Opportunities grouped by account
A dashboard filter that hides accounts with opportunities
A formula field on Account that counts its opportunities

explanation: The 'with or without' relationship in a custom report type includes parents that have no children.

stem: Two blocks of data from different report types must be shown side by side in one report. Which format fits?

options.text: A joined report
A matrix report
A tabular report
A summary report

explanation: Joined reports combine blocks from multiple report types.
